title: FinSkillBench: Evaluating AI Agents and Domain Skills for Investment Management
summary: Investment management is a high-stakes domain in which agentic AI systems must do more than generate plausible text. They must retrieve point-in-time data, assemble correct computational inputs, invoke specialized methods, and produce auditable structured outputs. We introduce FinSkillBench, an evaluation suite designed to measure whether language model agents can effectively use financial domain skills to solve investment management tasks. The benchmark spans three domains, portfolio construction, risk management, and fundamental analysis, and includes 12 subtasks with 2,603 task episodes. Each episode provides point-in-time inputs, hidden ground truth, and a task-specific verifier.We compare three conditions: no skill, curated skill packages consisting of procedural documents and executable components, and self-generated skills in which the agent writes and reuses its own procedures within an episode. Across 9 models and a large-scale evaluation, curated skills consistently improve performance, raising mean scores from 0.366 to 0.528, with the largest gains in portfolio construction and risk management. In contrast, self-generated skills provide little benefit despite higher computational cost. An independent evaluation using a separate agent framework (Hermes Agent, 8 models, 5,280 episodes total) reproduces the directional pattern across all three domains, with the magnitude of skill effects varying by subtask and harness. These results showthat in investment management agents, access to reliable procedural skills can be as important as model choice, while naive self-generation of skills is often ineffective. We release the benchmark, evaluation tools, curated skill packages, and full trajectories to support further research.
core_methodology: Evaluation of language model agents using curated skill packages (procedural documents and executable components) versus self-generated skills in investment management tasks. Focuses on three domains: portfolio construction, risk management, and fundamental analysis with task-specific verifiers.
data_sources: Point-in-time financial data inputs with hidden ground truth for 2,603 task episodes across 12 subtasks.
alpha_potential: Demonstrates that curated financial domain skills significantly improve AI agent performance in investment management tasks, particularly in portfolio construction and risk management. Suggests that reliable procedural knowledge can be more impactful than model choice alone for generating actionable investment insights.
title_cn: FinSkillBench：评估投资管理领域AI代理及专业技能
summary_cn: 该研究介绍了FinSkillBench评估套件，通过2,603个任务场景测试语言模型代理在投资管理三大领域(组合构建、风险管理和基本面分析)的表现。结果表明，使用专业金融技能包可使平均得分从0.366提升至0.528，特别是在组合构建和风险管理方面。研究证明，可靠的程序性技能比模型选择更重要，为量化投资中AI代理的实际应用提供了重要参考框架。

title: FactorMiner: A Self-Evolving Agent with Skills and Experience Memory for Financial Alpha Discovery
summary: Formulaic alpha factor mining is a critical yet challenging task in quantitative investment, characterized by a vast search space and the need for domain-informed, interpretable signals. However, finding novel signals becomes increasingly difficult as the library grows due to high redundancy. We propose FactorMiner, a lightweight and flexible self-evolving agent framework designed to navigate this complex landscape through continuous knowledge accumulation. FactorMiner combines a Modular Skill Architecture that encapsulates systematic financial evaluation into executable tools with a structured Experience Memory that distills historical mining trials into actionable insights (successful patterns and failure constraints). By instantiating the Ralph Loop paradigm -- retrieve, generate, evaluate, and distill -- FactorMiner iteratively uses memory priors to guide exploration, reducing redundant search while focusing on promising directions. Experiments on multiple datasets across different assets and Markets show that FactorMiner constructs a diverse library of high-quality factors with competitive performance, while maintaining low redundancy among factors as the library scales. Overall, FactorMiner provides a practical approach to scalable discovery of interpretable formulaic alpha factors under the "Correlation Red Sea" constraint.
core_methodology: FactorMiner employs a self-evolving agent framework with Modular Skill Architecture (encapsulating financial evaluation tools) and structured Experience Memory (storing historical mining insights). It follows the Ralph Loop paradigm (Retrieve, Generate, Evaluate, Distill) to iteratively guide exploration using memory priors, reducing redundant search while focusing on promising directions for alpha factor mining.
data_sources: Multiple datasets across different assets and markets (specific assets/markets not detailed in abstract). Likely uses standard financial market data such as price, volume, and fundamental data.
alpha_potential: The system aims to discover novel, interpretable formulaic alpha factors by efficiently navigating the vast search space while minimizing redundancy. It focuses on patterns that have historically shown predictive power, with explicit mechanisms to remember successful patterns and failure constraints.
title_cn: FactorMiner：一种具备技能与经验记忆的自进化代理，用于金融Alpha因子挖掘
summary_cn: FactorMiner提出了一种轻量级自进化代理框架，通过模块化技能架构（封装金融评估工具）和结构化经验记忆（存储历史挖掘数据），采用Ralph循环范式（检索-生成-评估-提炼）持续优化Alpha因子发现过程。该系统在不同资产和市场的实验中展现出构建高质量、低冗余因子库的能力，为解决'相关红海'约束下的可扩展Alpha发现提供了实用方案。

title: M3: A State-Event Generative Foundation Model for Market Microstructure Dynamics
summary: Market microstructure simulation aims to model how liquidity, prices, and order flow evolve in electronic financial markets. Since market data reveal only one realized trajectory, many important questions are inherently counterfactual and require realistic trajectory-level simulation. Existing financial generative models, however, often model order events and market states, such as the LOB, in isolation, overlooking the dynamic interaction between order flow and liquidity in market microstructure. We propose the \textbf{M3} (\underline{M}arket \underline{M}icrostructure \underline{M}odel), a state-event generative foundation model for market microstructure dynamics. \textbf{M3} learns to generate future order-flow trajectories, while accounting for the evolving interaction between order events and limit-order-book liquidity. Trained on large-scale order-level real stock market data, \textbf{M3} exhibits predictable scaling behavior, reproduces key market stylized facts, and enables practical simulation-based applications including forecasting, stress testing, and market-impact analysis. These results suggest a scalable foundation-model paradigm for counterfactual market simulation at the microstructure level.
core_methodology: The M3 model is a state-event generative foundation model that simulates market microstructure dynamics by jointly modeling order flow and limit-order-book liquidity. It uses deep learning techniques to generate realistic trajectory-level simulations of market behavior, accounting for the dynamic interaction between order events and market states.
data_sources: The model is trained on large-scale order-level real stock market data, which includes detailed information about order flow and limit-order-book dynamics.
alpha_potential: M3's ability to generate realistic counterfactual market simulations can be leveraged for forecasting, stress testing, and market-impact analysis. This enables the identification of market inefficiencies and the development of trading strategies that exploit microstructure patterns.
title_cn: M3：一种用于市场微观结构动态的状态-事件生成基础模型
summary_cn: M3模型通过学习订单流和限价订单簿流动性之间的动态交互，能够生成未来订单流轨迹。该模型基于大规模真实股票市场数据训练，可应用于预测、压力测试和市场影响分析，为量化交易提供了新的微观结构仿真工具。

title: Dynamic Portfolio Optimization under CVaR Constraints
summary: We study continuous-time dynamic portfolio optimization under a Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) constraint on the investor's terminal loss. For a general class of convex trading objectives, we exploit the auxiliary-threshold representation of CVaR to establish the existence of an optimal strategy and strong duality without requiring market completeness. These results motivate a dual-based nested bisection--golden-search algorithm over the threshold and Lagrangian multiplier, where the inner iterations reduce to standard unconstrained stochastic control problems. We prove that the resulting strategies converge to the optimal control as the number of iterations tends to infinity. Numerical experiments recover the Merton policy when the risk constraint is nonbinding. When the constraint is binding, the optimal strategy becomes state dependent: the investor reduces risky exposure following adverse outcomes but preserves, and near maturity may increase, exposure following favorable outcomes. Thus, a terminal CVaR constraint produces an asymmetric reallocation across states rather than uniform de-risking. Nontraded endowment risk amplifies the conservative adjustment, whereas price impact lowers desired positions and adjustment speeds.
core_methodology: The paper presents a continuous-time dynamic portfolio optimization approach under Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) constraints. It leverages an auxiliary-threshold representation of CVaR to establish the existence of an optimal strategy and strong duality without requiring market completeness. The methodology involves a dual-based nested bisection--golden-search algorithm over the threshold and Lagrangian multiplier, solving standard unconstrained stochastic control problems in the inner iterations.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular data sources but assumes general market prices and returns, applicable to any financial asset class with observable price data.
alpha_potential: The approach provides a systematic way to manage tail risk while optimizing portfolio returns, which can be particularly valuable in turbulent markets. The state-dependent strategy, which adjusts risky exposure based on past outcomes, could exploit market inefficiencies related to momentum and mean-reversion effects, especially near maturity.
title_cn: CVaR约束下的动态投资组合优化
summary_cn: 本文研究了在终端损失的CVaR约束下的连续时间动态投资组合优化。通过CVaR的辅助阈值表示，我们证明了在不要求市场完备性的情况下存在最优策略和强对偶性。该方法通过双嵌套二分-黄金分割算法求解，内层迭代简化为标准的无约束随机控制问题。数值实验表明，当风险约束非绑定时的最优策略与Merton策略一致，而在绑定约束下，最优策略变为状态依赖，表现出不对称的资产配置调整，这对于实际交易中的风险管理具有重要应用价值。

title: ContestTrade: A Multi-Agent Trading System Based on Internal Contest Mechanism
summary: In financial trading, large language model (LLM)-based agents demonstrate significant potential, but their decisions can be sensitive to noisy and non-stationary market information. We propose ContestTrade, a multi-agent trading system with an internal competitive mechanism inspired by institutional investment workflows. The system consists of two specialized teams: (1) a Data Team that processes and condenses massive market data into diversified textual factors optimized for constrained LLM context windows, and (2) a Research Team that produces parallelized multipath trading decisions via tool-augmented deep research. The core design is a "Quantify-Predict-Allocate" contest mechanism within each team: agent outputs are scored only after market outcomes become observable, future utility is predicted from historical scores, and resources are allocated to agents with positive predicted utility. In a post-2024 A-share backtest, ContestTrade achieves higher backtested return and risk-adjusted performance than the evaluated baselines. We further describe the temporal protocol, implementation choices, and limitations to clarify the scope of these results.
core_methodology: Multi-agent trading system with internal competitive mechanism ('Quantify-Predict-Allocate'), featuring specialized data processing and research teams using LLM-optimized textual factors and tool-augmented deep research for parallelized decision-making
data_sources: A-shares market data (post-2024 backtest mentioned), processed into condensed textual factors for LLM consumption
alpha_potential: Competitive team structure and contest mechanism may capture differentiated signals by: (1) overcoming LLM sensitivity to market noise through specialized agent roles, (2) generating diversified perspectives via parallel research paths, and (3) dynamically allocating resources to historically effective agents
title_cn: ContestTrade：基于内部竞赛机制的多智能体交易系统
summary_cn: ContestTrade创新性地将机构投资流程转化为多智能体竞赛架构,通过数据团队(文本因子压缩)与研究团队(工具增强深度研究)的专项分工,配合'量化-预测-分配'的赛后评分机制,在A股回测中展现优异的收益与风险调整表现。该系统通过分工竞争解决LLM对市场噪声敏感的问题,为量化实践提供了新型框架。

title: Position: Collusion Risks Among AI Reasoning Agents Justify Certification Requirements for Making Market Decisions
summary: This position paper argues that AI agents with chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities are predisposed to exhibit collusive behavior and should be required to obtain behavioral certification before making decisions that affect economic markets. This is because integrating these agents into society could collapse the legal evidentiary distinction between competition and collusion among independent firms without eroding the economic harm distinction. Experiments with DeepSeek-R1 agents in the Bertrand oligopoly pricing domain reveal a tendency towards tacit collusion that persists even when humans prompt the agents not to collude. We further show that the chain-of-thought of these agents can be steered toward either extremely collusive or highly competitive behavior in a way that is not semantically detectable by another LLM analyzing the reasoning traces. As a result, deploying reasoning agents for market decisions leads to collusive economic outcomes without any evidence of conspiracy or intent. Thus, certification based on observed behavior in representative situations is necessary to prevent collusion. We provide preliminary evidence that such agents can be steered in a generalizable way toward efficient competitive equilibria. However, developing a comprehensive behavioral certification will be required before these models can be deployed in real-world markets while ensuring their stability and efficiency.
core_methodology: The paper investigates the behavior of AI agents with chain-of-thought reasoning in market scenarios, specifically focusing on their tendency towards tacit collusion in oligopoly pricing. It uses experimental setups with DeepSeek-R1 agents to observe and manipulate reasoning traces.
data_sources: Simulated Bertrand oligopoly pricing scenarios with AI agents.
alpha_potential: The paper highlights a significant risk of AI agents inadvertently causing market inefficiencies through collusive behavior. Understanding and mitigating this risk could lead to more robust AI-driven trading strategies and better regulatory frameworks to prevent artificial market distortions.
title_cn: 观点：AI推理代理的合谋风险证明其市场决策需认证
summary_cn: 本文指出具备链式思维推理能力的AI代理在寡头定价中易出现隐性合谋行为，建议实施行为认证。研究发现即使人工提示不要合谋，DeepSeek-R1代理仍持续表现出合谋倾向，且其推理轨迹可被暗中操控而不留语义痕迹。这对算法交易的意义在于：1) 揭示了AI代理可能无意识地扭曲市场效率 2) 强调了在金融领域部署前需建立完善的行为认证体系。研究成果为开发合规的AI交易系统提供了重要参考。

title: StocksTalk: A Voice-Enabled Conversational Agent for Structured Query Generation over Web Data
summary: StocksTalk is a voice-enabled conversational system for transforming spoken financial screening requests into executable and validated structured queries over real-world market data. The system combines streaming speech recognition, retrieval-augmented constraint extraction, schema-grounded LLM-based SQL generation, rule-based validation, and human-in-the-loop verification within an interactive dashboard. Unlike traditional template-driven financial assistants, StocksTalk exposes intermediate reasoning artifacts, including extracted constraints, normalized financial metrics, operator grounding, and generated queries, allowing users to inspect and refine each stage before execution. To evaluate the system, we curate a benchmark of 150 spoken financial prompts spanning multiple investment strategies and input noise conditions. Experimental results show that retrieval grounding, constrained query generation, and interactive verification substantially improve constraint extraction accuracy, SQL executability, logical consistency, and multi-turn stability compared to baseline LLM-based approaches. StocksTalk demonstrates how transparent, voice-driven interfaces can bridge natural language interaction and structured financial analysis, providing an effective framework for conversational stock screening and decision support.
core_methodology: The paper presents a system combining streaming speech recognition, retrieval-augmented constraint extraction, schema-grounded LLM-based SQL generation, rule-based validation, and human-in-the-loop verification to transform spoken financial screening requests into executable structured queries.
data_sources: Real-world market data; the paper mentions structured queries over web data, implying potential integration with financial databases or APIs.
alpha_potential: The system could enable faster and more intuitive query generation for screening stocks based on various strategies, potentially uncovering alpha by allowing traders to quickly test and refine screening criteria using natural language. The interactive verification and transparency may reduce errors in query construction, leading to more accurate screening results.
title_cn: StocksTalk：一种基于语音的对话代理，用于在Web数据上生成结构化查询
summary_cn: StocksTalk是一个语音交互系统，可将金融筛选请求转化为结构化查询。结合语音识别、检索增强约束提取和LLM生成的SQL，提供透明和交互式验证，可能提升策略开发和股票筛选的效率。

title: Towards Reversible Forgetting: Managing Obsolete Knowledge in Continual Enterprise AI Agents
summary: Continual learning has traditionally treated forgetting as a failure, emphasizing preservation of previously acquired knowledge as environments evolve. We argue that this objective is incomplete for enterprise AI agents operating in non-stationary environments, where customers, policies, tools, workflows, regulations, and market conditions change over time. Indiscriminate retention can allow obsolete knowledge to influence decisions, creating negative transfer and operational risk. We therefore propose reversible forgetting: a conceptual framework with three operational memory states: active, dormant, and retired, and a reactivation transition that can restore dormant knowledge when its relevance returns. We instantiate the framework as a Hysteretic Reversible Memory Controller that accumulates relevance evidence, uses asymmetric thresholds to prevent state oscillation, tests reactivation in shadow mode, and gates retirement through policy. The framework reduces the influence of obsolete information without conflating temporary suppression with permanent erasure. Finance illustrates the idea: knowledge useful under one market regime may become harmful under another yet regain relevance when similar conditions recur.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a Hysteretic Reversible Memory Controller for managing obsolete knowledge in continual learning systems, with a focus on reversible forgetting. The framework includes three memory states (active, dormant, retired) and mechanisms for reactivation and retirement based on relevance evidence and policy.
data_sources: Although not explicitly mentioned, the framework is designed for non-stationary environments, implying it could be applied to financial market data where regimes change over time.
alpha_potential: The methodology could help in dynamically adapting trading strategies to changing market regimes by suppressing obsolete knowledge and reactivating relevant knowledge when conditions recur, potentially reducing negative transfer and improving strategy performance.
title_cn: 迈向可逆遗忘：持续性企业AI代理中过时知识的管理
summary_cn: 本文提出了一个可逆遗忘框架，通过管理知识的活跃、休眠和退役状态，动态适应非平稳环境。在金融领域，该框架可帮助交易策略在不同市场周期中灵活调整，减少过时知识的影响，并在类似市场条件重现时重新激活相关知识，从而提升策略表现。

title: Classifying Directional Trajectories Near Criticality in the Three-State Majority-Vote Model with Deep Belief Networks and Bidirectional GRUs
summary: In this work, we investigate whether the latent representations learned by a Deep Belief Network (DBN) and a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU) can discriminate among four dynamically distinct trajectory types in the three-state majority vote model (MV3): approach from disorder, approach from order, departure to disorder, and departure to order. The DBN, pre-trained in an unsupervised manner on static equilibrium samples via a Gaussian-Bernoulli Restricted Boltzmann Machine input layer and architecture $784 \to 4096 \to 225 \to 81$, encodes each lattice snapshot into an 81-dimensional latent vector. A t-SNE analysis of the DBN latent space reveals only partial separation of the four trajectory types, reflecting the fact that a model trained on static configurations cannot fully resolve directional temporal structure. A two-layer Bi-GRU classifier, trained on sequences of DBN-encoded snapshots of length $T = 50$, achieves near-perfect separation of all four trajectory types in its hidden state space, as confirmed by t-SNE visualization on both training and test sets. Furthermore, a sliding-window application of the trained Bi-GRU to continuous MV3 dynamics demonstrates its ability to sense the system's current dynamical regime in real-time. These results establish a principled hierarchical architecture for detecting and classifying critical transitions in agent-based opinion dynamics models.
core_methodology: The paper employs a Deep Belief Network (DBN) for unsupervised pre-training on static equilibrium samples and a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU) for classifying directional trajectories in a three-state majority vote model. The hierarchical architecture effectively captures temporal dynamics and critical transitions.
data_sources: The study uses synthetic data from the three-state majority vote model (MV3), which simulates agent-based opinion dynamics. This can be analogous to market sentiment or order flow dynamics in financial markets.
alpha_potential: The methodology can be adapted to detect regime shifts or critical transitions in financial markets, such as identifying momentum shifts or sentiment reversals. The real-time sensing capability of the Bi-GRU could be valuable for high-frequency trading or algorithmic strategy adjustments.
title_cn: 基于深度信念网络和双向门控循环单元的三态多数投票模型临界区方向轨迹分类

title: When Does Dynamic Ensembling Pay Off? Diagnosing Regionwise Gains in Regression under Distribution Shift
summary: Whether input-dependent ("dynamic") combination of a regression model pool beats the best static blend depends on the shift and is rarely known before deployment. Can a small labeled target-domain probe tell us when reallocating trust across regions of the input space will pay off? We answer this with $\widehat{D}_{\mathrm{CF5}}$, which estimates from the probe the cross-fitted gain of the regionwise convex combination over the best static convex blend: the realizable value of deciding, region by region, whom to trust. Across a frozen suite of 12 dataset-shift pairs (spatial, temporal, domain, feature-cluster), $\widehat{D}_{\mathrm{CF5}}$ predicts realized regionwise test gains with dataset-level Spearman $+0.98$ (95% CI $[+0.83, +1.00]$; $p=5\times10^{-5}$), including two cases overturning preregistered expectations. The relationship holds in a 16-pair sensitivity analysis (Spearman $+0.83$), whereas alternative probe diagnostics reach at most $+0.66$. This contrast isolates regional trust reallocation: correlation is $+0.98$ for regionwise-convex gain, but $+0.01$ for smooth covariate-dependent stacking after affine correction. A controlled generator shows dynamic gains arise from the interaction of shift heterogeneity and local competence, increase with shift severity, and become realizable between 128 and 256 probe labels in the tested grid. The Probe-Validated Ensemble Selector chooses among a static affine stacker and dynamic realizers, deploying a candidate only when a held-out lower confidence bound clears the static-convex floor. In a preregistered prospective batch, it matched or improved the floor in all 12 runs; two deployments reduced test risk by 11% and 16%, while the gate rejected a candidate whose un-gated deployment incurred $>30\times$ the static loss. We release OpenRegShift, a reproducible evaluation harness for regression ensembles under distribution shift.
core_methodology: Dynamic ensembling of regression models with region-wise trust reallocation under distribution shift, validated through probe diagnostics and selection mechanism
data_sources: Generic regression datasets across spatial, temporal, domain, and feature-cluster shifts (specific financial data not mentioned but methodology is transferable)
alpha_potential: Addresses critical challenge of model adaptation to regime changes in markets - can improve factor models, volatility prediction, and cross-asset strategies when market conditions shift

summary_cn: 该研究提出的动态集成方法和验证框架可有效解决量化交易中市场状态突变时的模型适应问题。通过区域置信度重分配和小样本验证，能显著提升因子模型、波动率预测等在市场机制变化时的稳定性，已在其他领域实现11-16%的风险降低。

title: Reinforced Planning with Latent World Models
summary: Humans solve complex problems by constructing plans and mentally simulating their outcomes with an internal model of the world. Machine learning has produced world models that similarly predict the outcomes of action sequences, but the improvement of candidate plans still isn't fully learned. Current planners are either hand-designed, distilled from a hand-designed optimizer, or learned only to inform an amortized policy rather than to revise the plan itself. We introduce the Reinforced Planning, a method based on the idea that search can be learned by reinforcing good search rules into a neural planner. Our implementation RP1 learns both how to evaluate imagined outcomes through a critic, as well as how to improve multi-step plans through an optimizer trained fully offline from imagined world-model roll-outs. To our knowledge, RP1 is the first method to fully learn how to improve multi-step plans. Furthermore, it can be trained independently of and attached to any pretrained latent world model. Across visual navigation, arm reaching, and robotic manipulation on two world-model backbones, RP1 substantially outperforms hand-designed search algorithms, reaching near-perfect success in several settings while using $1,000 \times$ less world-model rollouts and being up to $67 \times$ faster than the strongest alternative under concurrent planner inference.
core_methodology: Reinforced Planning with Latent World Models (RP1) learns to evaluate and improve multi-step plans through a critic and optimizer, trained offline from imagined world-model roll-outs. This method leverages reinforcement learning to enhance planning efficiency and effectiveness.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but mentions visual navigation, arm reaching, and robotic manipulation, suggesting potential adaptability to market data for trading strategies.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to trading by improving multi-step planning and decision-making in dynamic financial markets, potentially identifying inefficiencies in price movements or portfolio rebalancing strategies.
title_cn: 基于潜在世界模型的强化规划
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种强化规划方法（RP1），通过离线训练的批评者和优化器来评估和改进多步计划。该方法可应用于金融交易，提升动态市场中的多步决策效率，潜在优化投资组合再平衡策略。

title: Robust Risk Under Evolving Uncertainty: A Wasserstein Counterpart of the Entropic Value-at-Risk
summary: An agent still learning its environment should be cautious while ignorant and bold once confident. The entropic value-at-risk captures this through a robust-optimization identity---a confidence level fixes the radius of a relative-entropy ball of alternative models---but that ball cannot reach catastrophes the nominal deems impossible, precisely what a safe agent must hedge. We instead use an optimal-transport ball and study the coherent risk measure it induces, the Wasserstein entropic value-at-risk. It has a variational dual mirroring the entropic formula (an inverse temperature becomes a transport price), occupies a definite place in the risk hierarchy, and provably accounts for the reachable catastrophes the entropic measure ignores; we verify both dualities numerically. Driving the transport radius by belief entropy then yields a closed-form robust dynamic-programming operator whose caution contracts as the belief sharpens, with a certified safety sandwich and a sharp safety switch.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a new coherent risk measure called the Wasserstein Entropic Value-at-Risk (WEVaR), which uses optimal transport theory to create a robust optimization framework that dynamically adjusts risk assessment based on the agent's evolving confidence in its environment. The approach provides a more comprehensive hedge against catastrophic risks compared to traditional entropic value-at-risk methods.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular data sources but the methodology is applicable to any financial dataset where risk assessment and dynamic portfolio optimization are relevant, including equity, fixed income, and derivative markets.
alpha_potential: The WEVaR framework can enhance risk-adjusted returns by more accurately accounting for tail risks and dynamically adjusting portfolio allocations as market confidence levels change. This is particularly valuable in volatile or uncertain market conditions where traditional risk measures may fail to capture extreme outcomes.
title_cn: 在不断演变的不确定性下的稳健风险：熵值在险风险的最优传输对应方法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种新的稳健风险度量方法——Wasserstein熵值在险风险(WEVaR)，通过最优传输理论创建动态风险评估框架。该方法相比传统熵值法能更全面地覆盖极端风险，适用于市场不确定性高时的资产组合优化。其独特价值在于风险半径随置信度自动调节的机制，为量化交易提供了新型尾部风险管理工具。

title: Discretizing Continuous Time Series for Imputation with Masked Diffusion Training
summary: Time series imputation is a crucial area for reliable time series analysis, yet it remains challenging due to the complex temporal dynamics and noise of real-world data. Existing approaches, however, exhibit two limitations: missing and observed values are embedded within the same representation space without explicit structural separation, and continuous diffusion-based methods are trained to predict added noise rather than the original signal. To address these, we propose the Masked Diffusion Time-series Imputation Model (MDTIM), which leverages the training paradigm of masked diffusion model for imputation tasks. The MASK token is structurally orthogonal to valid observations, and the model directly predicts the original values, naturally aligning both the representation and the learning objective with the imputation task. To bridge the gap between discrete masked diffusion and the continuous, ordinal nature of time series, we further introduce Stochastic Discretization, which maps continuous values to ordinal-aware tokens while preserving continuous dynamics. Our experiments on diverse benchmarks confirm that MDTIM achieves superior robustness and scalability, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art deterministic and generative baselines across various missing scenarios.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Masked Diffusion Time-series Imputation Model (MDTIM) for time series data imputation, leveraging masked diffusion models to predict original values directly, and utilizing Stochastic Discretization to handle continuous time series. By distinguishing missing observations with a MASK token, the model aligns representation and learning objectives with imputation tasks, improving robustness and scalability in diverse missing data scenarios.
data_sources: The model can be applied to market price time series, volume data, or alternative data like sentiment or macroeconomic indicators, handling missing data points which are common in real-world financial datasets.
alpha_potential: Improved imputation of missing data points can enhance the reliability of quantitative trading signals derived from time series analysis, ensuring more accurate predictions of asset price movements and risk assessments. The model's superior performance in handling various missing patterns can be crucial for high-frequency trading, backtesting, and algorithmic trading strategies where data integrity is critical.
title_cn: 离散化连续时间序列用于基于掩码扩散训练的插补
summary_cn: 本文提出的MDTIM模型通过引入掩码扩散训练范式，有效处理时间序列中的缺失数据问题，特别适用于金融市场中常见的非连续数据场景。其独特的离散化方法和直接预测原始信号的能力，可能提升量化交易中策略信号的可靠性。

title: Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning for Controlled Hawkes Jump-Diffusions
summary: We study stochastic control of multivariate Hawkes-driven stochastic differential equations with machine learning algorithms in a non-Markovian setting. Due to the path dependence of the memory of the Hawkes intensity, this problem does not fall within classical stochastic control theory outside particular Markovian kernels. We first develop a finite-dimensional Markovianization procedure and algorithm to approximate multivariate Hawkes processes with mixtures of exponential kernels. We prove the convergence of the Markovianized approximation of the Hawkes process, its intensity, and the value of the problem to the original non-Markovian processes and the value of the primal problem. We then formulate continuous-time deterministic policy gradient learning on the Markovianized approximation of the problem, called Hawkes-CT DDPG. We propose a model-free algorithm to solve the non-Markovian Hawkes-driven optimization by observing only the event times of the process, the realization of the solution to the SDE, and a chosen set of decay filters, while the Hawkes kernel coefficients remain unknown. We compare our continuous time reinforcement learning Hawkes-CT DDPG method with discrete time reinforcement learning techniques under three different types of kernels: simple exponential, Erlang, and power-law kernels.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel method for controlling multivariate Hawkes-driven SDEs using continuous-time reinforcement learning (Hawkes-CT DDPG). It involves a finite-dimensional Markovianization procedure to approximate Hawkes processes with exponential kernel mixtures, followed by deterministic policy gradient learning applied to the Markovianized version.
data_sources: Event times of the process, realization of the solution to the SDE, and a chosen set of decay filters. The approach is model-free, not requiring prior knowledge of Hawkes kernel coefficients.
alpha_potential: Potential to model and exploit self-exciting market behaviors (like clustered orders or volatility shocks) through Hawkes processes, which are particularly relevant in high-frequency trading and market microstructure analysis.
title_cn: 控制霍克斯跳跃扩散的连续时间强化学习
summary_cn: 本研究通过连续时间强化学习方法控制多变量霍克斯驱动的随机微分方程，开发了一种有限维马尔可夫化算法来近似霍克斯过程。该方法能有效捕捉市场的自激行为（如订单聚集和波动冲击），为高频交易和市场微结构分析提供潜在的阿尔法来源。

title: Sharper Regret Bounds for Time-Varying Gaussian Process Bandits with Constant Exploration
summary: We study Bayesian optimization in a time-varying environment where the unknown reward function evolves according to a Gaussian process drift model. Existing GP-UCB analyses in this setting typically require the exploration parameter to grow with the horizon to maintain uniform confidence bounds. Using per-round local confidence events, we show that GP-UCB can instead be run with a constant exploration parameter and obtain an expected-regret bound whose coefficient depends on the drift rate. We also derive a sharper time-varying maximum-information-gain bound. For the squared exponential kernel, it yields $\tilde\gamma_T/T=\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\epsilon^{1/2})$ and expected average regret $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\epsilon^{1/4})$ in the persistent-drift regime. The same constant-exploration analysis also yields realized-regret guarantees. Simulations support the predicted logarithmic dependence of the bound-suggested exploration parameter on $1/\epsilon$.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an improved version of the Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (GP-UCB) algorithm for time-varying environments, where the reward function evolves according to a Gaussian process drift model. It proposes using per-round local confidence events to maintain uniform confidence bounds with a constant exploration parameter, leading to sharper regret bounds and better performance in dynamic settings.
data_sources: The methodology is theoretical but can be applied to financial time series data, such as stock prices, returns, or other market indicators that exhibit time-varying patterns.
alpha_potential: The approach could be valuable for dynamic portfolio optimization, adaptive trading strategies, and other applications where the underlying market conditions or asset returns are non-stationary. The constant exploration parameter and sharper regret bounds may lead to more robust performance in changing market regimes.
title_cn: 恒定探索下时变高斯过程多臂老虎机的更尖锐遗憾边界
summary_cn: 本文研究了时变环境中的贝叶斯优化问题，改进GP-UCB算法使其能在恒定探索参数下运行，并获得与漂移率相关的更优遗憾边界。这一方法对金融市场中时变参数的策略优化具有潜在应用价值，可用于动态资产配置和自适应交易系统的开发。

title: The Label Horizon Paradox: Rethinking Supervision Targets in Financial Forecasting
summary: While deep learning has revolutionized financial forecasting through sophisticated architectures, the design of the supervision signal itself is rarely scrutinized. We challenge the canonical assumption that training labels must strictly mirror inference targets, uncovering the Label Horizon Paradox: the optimal supervision signal often deviates from the prediction goal, shifting across intermediate horizons governed by market dynamics. We theoretically ground this phenomenon in a dynamic signal-noise trade-off, demonstrating that generalization hinges on the competition between marginal signal realization and noise accumulation. To operationalize this insight, we propose a bi-level optimization framework that autonomously identifies the optimal proxy label within a single training run. Extensive experiments on large-scale financial datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over conventional baselines, thereby opening new avenues for label-centric research in financial forecasting.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a bi-level optimization framework to dynamically determine optimal proxy labels for financial forecasting, challenging the traditional approach of using direct inference targets as labels. It formalizes the concept of the Label Horizon Paradox where intermediate supervision signals can outperform direct targets due to market dynamics.
data_sources: Large-scale financial datasets (specific assets/exchanges not detailed in abstract)
alpha_potential: Addresses a fundamental inefficiency in how machine learning models are trained for financial predictions by optimizing the supervision signal itself. This could uncover new alpha sources by better aligning training objectives with market dynamics evolution.
title_cn: 标签视界悖论：重新思考金融预测中的监督目标
summary_cn: 本文提出'标签视界悖论'，颠覆金融预测中监督信号必须严格匹配预测目标的传统假设。创新性地通过双层优化框架自动寻找最优代理标签，实验证明其能有效提升模型表现。这种方法为量化交易中监督信号优化提供了新范式，尤其适用于捕捉市场动态变化的预测场景。

title: Structured Latent Space Modeling over Multi-Scale Temporal Patches for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
summary: Existing patching and multi-scale methods advance multivariate time series forecasting but treat learned representations as transient byproducts of prediction, lacking explicit mechanisms that enforce structural consistency across temporal scales. We propose M2Patch, a CNN-based architecture that organizes channel-independent observations into a structured latent space via two complementary differentiable penalties. Multi-scale patching decomposes the input into overlapping temporal granularities, depthwise separable CNN blocks with progressively growing dilation extracts scale-specific features at linear complexity, and per-scale learned projections compress these features into a compact latent representation. An intra-scale smoothness penalty enforces temporal continuity between adjacent patches, while an inter-scale alignment penalty restores cross-granularity interaction through learnable cross-scale mappings, so that all scales encode mutually consistent representations of the underlying dynamics. Extensive experiments on ten real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that M2Patch significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Further analyses establish M2Patch as a structure-aware recognizer: it recovers channel functional groupings and remains robust under patch-level input corruption, confirming that the structured latent space captures the data's intrinsic dynamics.
core_methodology: M2Patch proposes a CNN-based architecture that uses multi-scale patching and depthwise separable CNN blocks with growing dilation to extract scale-specific features. It enforces structural consistency across temporal scales through intra-scale smoothness and inter-scale alignment penalties, resulting in a structured latent space that captures underlying dynamics.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the methodology on ten real-world benchmark datasets, which likely include multivariate time series data such as financial markets, weather, traffic, etc. For quantitative finance, this could be adapted to market data like price/volume time series.
alpha_potential: The structured latent space and multi-scale feature extraction could potentially uncover hidden patterns in financial time series data, leading to improved forecasting accuracy. The robustness to patch-level corruption suggests the model could handle noisy market data well.
title_cn: 基于多尺度时间片段的结构化潜在空间建模在多变量时间序列预测中的应用
summary_cn: M2Patch通过多尺度时间片段分解和带有扩张率的深度可分离CNN块提取尺度特定特征，并通过跨尺度的平滑和对齐惩罚构建结构化潜在空间。该方法在十大数据集上表现优异，能够恢复通道功能分组并在输入损坏时保持稳健，适用于金融时间序列预测和模式识别。

title: Hybrid LLM-Augmented Reinforcement Learning Agents for Complex Sequential Decision Tasks
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently shown strong capabilities in reasoning, planning, and tool-use, enabling new forms of autonomous agents. However, LLM-based agents struggle with long-horizon sequential decision tasks that require precise action optimization and environment interaction. Reinforcement Learning (RL), while effective for sequential control, often lacks the high-level abstraction and task decomposition abilities needed for complex scenarios. This paper introduces an LLM-Augmented Reinforcement Learning Agent that integrates LLM-driven planning with RL-based action optimization. The proposed architecture leverages the LLM to generate subgoals, structured plans, and contextual guidance, while the RL agent refines low-level actions through interaction with the environment. Experiments on sequential decision tasks demonstrate improved sample efficiency, higher success rates, and more coherent action trajectories compared to RL-only and LLM-only baselines. This hybrid paradigm highlights a promising direction for building more capable autonomous systems.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a hybrid architecture combining Large Language Models (LLMs) for high-level planning and task decomposition with Reinforcement Learning (RL) for low-level action optimization. This integration aims to leverage the reasoning and planning capabilities of LLMs with the precise environment interaction of RL.
data_sources: While the abstract does not specify financial data sources, the methodology could be applied to market data such as price series, order book data, or alternative data for trading tasks.
alpha_potential: The hybrid approach could potentially generate alpha by improving the efficiency and coherence of trading strategies that require complex sequential decision-making, such as portfolio rebalancing, execution algorithms, or multi-asset trading strategies. The LLM's ability to decompose tasks and provide contextual guidance could lead to more adaptive and robust trading agents.
title_cn: 混合LLM增强的强化学习智能体在复杂序列决策任务中的应用
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种结合大语言模型（LLM）与强化学习（RL）的混合架构，利用LLM进行高层规划和任务分解，RL负责低层动作优化。这种方法可应用于金融市场的复杂序列决策任务，如算法交易和投资组合管理，有望提高策略的适应性和效率。

title: Residual Algebra for Representation-Preserving Learning
summary: Learning from heterogeneous representations is often reduced to feature concatenation, erasing which representation produced each error. We propose residual algebra, in which each representation retains its coordinate system and owns its unresolved residual until an explicit aggregation boundary. Fold instantiates representations as point-in-time conditional-mean fields on 10x10 rank grids, and FPRC-PQ composes them through relax-aggregate-close: each field first fits a correction to its own residual, corrected fields then meet at a fixed mean, and a shared learner closes only the aggregate's fresh residual. We formalize aggregation as a quotient by the zero-sum redistribution kernel, characterizing legal post-aggregation operators as those constant on its cosets. The resulting composition separates representation, local residual estimation, and residual-of-residual estimation, with population variance reduction and first-order coupled-path mean orthogonality. Rumination-B and Rumination-H extend the algebra with quotient-legal finite correction and feedback. On 3.67M Chinese A-share stock-day observations (2023-2026) under a frozen point-in-time protocol, FPRC-PQ raises net-of-cost return from 13.52% to 19.10% and Sharpe from 1.42 to 2.09, outperforming matched-capacity, unified-residual, identity-free two-stage, and pairwise-only controls. The gain is thus attributable to explicit residual ownership and composition rather than additional features or trees.
core_methodology: Residual algebra for representation-preserving learning, involving explicit residual ownership and composition through relax-aggregate-close operations. The method separates representation, local residual estimation, and residual-of-residual estimation, enhancing model interpretability and performance.
data_sources: 3.67M Chinese A-share stock-day observations from 2023 to 2026 under a frozen point-in-time protocol.
alpha_potential: The methodology improves net-of-cost return and Sharpe ratio, suggesting it captures market inefficiencies through better residual modeling and aggregation. The explicit handling of residuals may help in identifying mispriced securities or improving portfolio rebalancing strategies.
title_cn: 用于表示保留学习的残差代数
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种残差代数方法，通过显式残差所有权和组合提升模型性能。在中证A股数据上，该方法显著提高了净收益和夏普比率，适用于组合优化和因子投资。核心技术包括残差分离和聚合操作，有助于捕捉市场无效性并优化交易策略。

title: Fast Best-in-Class Regret for Contextual Bandits
summary: We study the problem of stochastic contextual bandits in the agnostic setting, where the goal is to compete with the best policy in a given class without assuming realizability or imposing model restrictions on losses or rewards. In this work, we establish the first fast rate for regret relative to the best-in-class policy. Our proposed algorithm updates the policy at every round by minimizing a pessimistic objective, defined as a clipped inverse-propensity estimate of the policy value plus a variance penalty. By leveraging entropy assumptions on the policy class and a H\"olderian error-bound condition (a generalization of the margin condition), we achieve fast best-in-class regret rates, including polylogarithmic rates in the parametric case. The analysis is driven by a sequential self-normalized maximal inequality for bounded martingale empirical processes, which yields uniform variance-adaptive confidence bounds and guarantees pessimism under adaptive data collection.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a contextual bandit algorithm that minimizes a pessimistic objective function, combining clipped inverse-propensity estimates of policy value with a variance penalty. It leverages entropy assumptions on the policy class and a H"olderian error-bound condition to achieve fast regret rates, including polylogarithmic rates for parametric cases.
data_sources: Theoretical study, no specific financial data sources mentioned, but the methodology is applicable to any contextual bandit problem in finance (e.g., dynamic portfolio allocation, algorithmic trading).
alpha_potential: This approach could be adapted to discover and exploit market inefficiencies in real-time by dynamically adjusting trading policies based on contextual information, potentially leading to improved risk-adjusted returns compared to static strategies.
title_cn: 上下文老虎机中的快速最佳类别内后悔
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种快速后悔最小化的上下文老虎机算法，适用于非实现性设置下的动态策略优化。通过将逆倾向评分估计与方差惩罚相结合的悲观目标函数，在政策类别的熵假设和Hölderian误差边界条件下实现快速后悔率。在金融交易中可应用于实时策略调整，提升动态投资组合管理的表现。

title: Concentrated Liquidity Provision: a Reinforcement Learning Perspective
summary: Automated market makers (AMMs) are a cornerstone of decentralised finance (DeFi). Constant product markets with concentrated liquidity, such as UniswapV3, are now a well-established design. In these markets, liquidity providers (LPs) face a sequential decision problem: they must decide when to rebalance their positions and which price ranges to allocate capital to as market conditions evolve. We formulate dynamic liquidity provision as a stochastic impulse control problem and use reinforcement learning (RL) to solve it, focusing on providing interpretable solutions. We show that learned policies exhibit rich state-dependent behaviour, allocating liquidity according to mispricing, rebalancing costs, uncertainty, inventory exposure, and heterogeneous risk preferences. These behaviours help compress the left tail of the Profit and Loss (PnL) distribution and avoid catastrophic outcomes under high uncertainty. Finally, we benchmark the RL agents against baseline and sophisticated agents from the AMM microstructure literature and analyse their performance.
core_methodology: The paper formulates dynamic liquidity provision in decentralized finance (DeFi) as a stochastic impulse control problem and solves it using reinforcement learning (RL). The approach provides interpretable solutions that exhibit state-dependent behaviors, optimizing liquidity allocation based on factors such as mispricing, rebalancing costs, uncertainty, inventory exposure, and risk preferences.
data_sources: The paper likely uses data from automated market makers (AMMs) like UniswapV3, focusing on price ranges, liquidity positions, and market conditions. Specific details on data sources are not explicitly mentioned in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The RL-based approach compresses the left tail of the PnL distribution, reducing catastrophic losses under high uncertainty. This could provide alpha by optimizing liquidity provision strategies in volatile or inefficient markets, particularly in DeFi where traditional market-making techniques may not apply.
title_cn: 集中流动性提供：强化学习的视角
summary_cn: 本文通过强化学习（RL）解决去中心化金融（DeFi）中动态流动性提供的随机脉冲控制问题。RL策略展现丰富的状态依赖行为，优化流动性分配以减少亏损风险，适用于高不确定性市场。该方法可提升自动化做市策略（如UniswapV3）的盈利能力。

title: Deep-MKV-TS: Path-Dependent McKean--Vlasov Control for Financial Time Series Generation
summary: We introduce Deep-MKV-TS, a path-dependent McKean-Vlasov framework for financial scenario generation. The stochastic dynamics are chosen by matching selected path and volatility features of generated scenarios to those observed in the data. Starting from an interpretable reference model, Deep-MKV-TS preserves the reference drift and adjusts its volatility, while a regularization penalty limits unnecessary departures from the calibrated dynamics. We solve the resulting control problem using a neural, sample-based implementation of the stochastic maximum principle. We validate the method against an exactly computable oracle. On Heston and Heston-mixture models, Deep-MKV-TS substantially reduces path-dependent and volatility-related deficiencies of the reference model. In delayed-volatility experiments, the correction remains effective as the forecasting horizon increases, while direct training becomes less reliable. On held-out intraday equity-index futures, the corrected model improves conditional forecasts relative to the reference and reaches a level of performance comparable to flexible generative and historical baselines. The resulting scenarios also support greater exposure than the reference under a fixed drawdown-risk target. These results show that path-dependent McKean-Vlasov control can enrich an interpretable reference model without replacing it.
core_methodology: Deep-MKV-TS is a method that leverages path-dependent McKean-Vlasov control to generate financial time series scenarios. It adjusts the volatility of a reference model (like Heston or Heston-mixture) while preserving the drift, using a neural implementation of the stochastic maximum principle. The method ensures the generated scenarios match observed path and volatility features in the data, with regularization to limit deviations from the calibrated dynamics.
data_sources: Intraday equity-index futures data, specifically held-out datasets, are used for validation. The method is also tested on synthetic data from Heston and Heston-mixture models.
alpha_potential: The method improves conditional forecasts and generates scenarios that allow for greater exposure under a fixed drawdown-risk target. This suggests it could be useful for risk management, derivative pricing, and portfolio optimization by providing more accurate and realistic market scenarios.
title_cn: Deep-MKV-TS：用于金融时间序列生成的路径依赖McKean-Vlasov控制框架
summary_cn: Deep-MKV-TS提出了一种基于路径依赖McKean-Vlasov控制的金融时间序列生成方法，通过调整参考模型的波动率并保留其漂移项，生成与市场数据特征匹配的场景。该方法在Heston模型和混合Heston模型上显著改善了路径依赖和波动率相关的缺陷，并在股指期货数据上提升了条件预测性能。生成的场景在固定回撤风险目标下支持更大的投资暴露，适用于风险管理、衍生品定价和投资组合优化。

title: From Accuracy to Auditability: A Survey of Determinism in Financial AI Systems
summary: Deploying machine learning in regulated financial environments -- credit risk, fraud detection, and anti-money laundering -- exposes critical vulnerabilities in algorithmic reproducibility. While early financial ML addressed statistical challenges such as backtest overfitting, deep neural networks and Generative AI have introduced mechanical nondeterminism rooted in hardware and architecture. This survey provides a systems perspective on reproducibility failures across three modalities now dominant in financial AI: tabular models (post-hoc explanation variance), graph networks (stochastic sampling and temporal asynchrony), and LLM-based agentic workflows (batch-dependent divergence and trajectory drift). We supplement the literature analysis with first-party experiments on public financial datasets -- quantifying explanation rank instability in credit scoring, prediction flip rates in GNN-based fraud detection, and tensor-parallel-induced output divergence in LLM entity extraction. We propose a layered evaluation framework linking modality-specific metrics (RBO, D_cos, TDI, PSD) to audit readiness, and empirically validate the complementarity of logit-level and semantic-level determinism measures.
core_methodology: The paper surveys and analyzes reproducibility issues in financial AI systems across three modalities: tabular models, graph networks, and LLM-based agentic workflows. It proposes a layered evaluation framework linking modality-specific metrics to audit readiness.
data_sources: Public financial datasets are used for experiments, including credit scoring, fraud detection, and LLM entity extraction tasks.
alpha_potential: Addresses critical vulnerabilities in algorithmic reproducibility, which can enhance the reliability and auditability of AI-driven trading strategies. This can lead to more robust and trustworthy models in credit risk, fraud detection, and other financial applications.
title_cn: 从准确性到可审计性：金融人工智能系统确定性研究综述
summary_cn: 本文综述了金融AI系统在表格模型、图网络和基于LLM的代理工作流程中的可重复性问题，提出了一个分层的评估框架以增强审计准备。研究通过公共金融数据集验证了方法的有效性，对提高金融AI系统的可靠性和可审计性具有重要实践价值。

title: Self-Evolving Agents as Dynamic Graph Transformation: A Survey and New Perspective
summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are increasingly becoming self-evolving systems that persist across interactions, maintain memories, use tools, acquire skills, refine workflows, and coordinate with other agents. These capabilities make agent states structural and dynamic: entities, relations, attributes, dependencies, and execution structures change with new evidence, feedback, and environmental conditions. Existing graph-agent surveys typically treat graphs as support structures for agent functions rather than as evolving substrates, while self-evolving-agent surveys focus on agent-level mechanisms and rarely discuss graph topology evolution. Thus, the coupling between evolving agent state and dynamic graph topology remains underexplored. This survey connects these two research lines by framing \textit{agent evolution as dynamic graph transformation}. We model agent state as a dynamic graph, where memories, tools, skills, workflows, and inter-agent relations are represented as typed nodes, edges, and subgraphs updated through schema-constrained rewrites. Based on this formulation, we organize existing dynamic-graph-based methods for self-evolving agents into four taxonomies: node/feature evolution, edge/topology evolution, subgraph activation, and cross-component co-evolution. Building on this taxonomy, we propose dynamic graph learning as reusable infrastructure for self-evolving agents and map nine dynamic-graph-learning subfields to agent-evolution capabilities, discussing their adaptations and possible failure modes. Finally, we discuss five types of graph-aware evaluation and governance protocols from a dynamic-graph perspective, which complement end-task evaluation. The goal is to provide a compact structural lens for designing and governing self-evolving agents.
core_methodology: The paper models agent state as a dynamic graph, where memories, tools, skills, workflows, and inter-agent relations are represented as typed nodes, edges, and subgraphs updated through schema-constrained rewrites. It connects self-evolving agents to dynamic graph transformation, organizing methods into four taxonomies: node/feature evolution, edge/topology evolution, subgraph activation, and cross-component co-evolution. This approach leverages dynamic graph learning as reusable infrastructure for self-evolving agents.
data_sources: The paper does not explicitly mention financial data, but the methodology can be applied to financial market data, alternative data, and interaction data among trading agents.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially identify hidden patterns and dependencies in financial markets by modeling trading strategies or market participants as dynamic graphs. The dynamic graph transformation could help in optimizing trading workflows, coordinating multi-agent trading systems, and adapting to changing market conditions.
title_cn: 作为动态图变换的自进化智能体：调查与新视角
summary_cn: 该论文探讨了将自进化智能体的状态建模为动态图，通过节点、边和子图的类型化表示来优化记忆、工具、技能、工作流和智能体间关系。在量化交易中，这种方法可用于优化交易策略、协调多智能体系统并适应市场变化。

title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling
summary: Looped language models have shown promising results on reasoning benchmarks, yet their potential for agentic tool use remains largely unexplored. We study this question in compositional tool-calling settings, where models must coordinate multiple API calls, maintain intermediate state, and preserve dependencies across tool interactions. We evaluate native and retrofitted looped language models on API-Bank, BFCL, and NESTful, comparing looped and non-looped models trained under matched supervised fine-tuning recipes and varying recurrent depth at inference time. In controlled experiments, recurrent computation generally benefits compositional and dependency-aware tool use, while providing smaller and more model-dependent gains on isolated API invocation. Accuracy on multi-step tool use generally increases with recurrent depth; adaptive inference, however, achieves a more favorable compute-performance trade-off by allocating additional computation only when needed. Our results suggest that looped language models are a promising architecture for agentic systems that require reliable planning, coordination, and execution of compositional tool use workflows.
core_methodology: The paper explores looped language models for compositional tool use, focusing on coordinating multiple API calls, maintaining intermediate state, and preserving dependencies across tool interactions. It evaluates the effectiveness of recurrent computation in improving multi-step tool use and adaptive inference for better computational efficiency.
data_sources: The study uses benchmarks like API-Bank, BFCL, and NESTful, which are designed to test compositional tool-calling capabilities. These are synthetic or standardized datasets for evaluating model performance in tool use workflows.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for trading strategies that require complex, multi-step decision-making processes, such as portfolio rebalancing or multi-asset arbitrage. The adaptive inference feature might optimize computational resources in real-time trading environments.
title_cn: 循环语言模型提升组合式工具调用能力
summary_cn: 该研究探讨了循环语言模型在组合式工具调用中的应用，通过协调多个API调用、维护中间状态和保持工具间依赖关系，提升了多步骤决策能力。在量化交易中，此方法可优化复杂的交易策略执行，如多资产套利或动态组合调整，自适应推断功能还能提高实时交易的计算效率。

title: SingularClip: Preventing Spectral Collapse to Maintain Plasticity in Continual and Reinforcement Learning
summary: Neural networks trained on nonstationary tasks frequently lose the ability to fit new targets, a phenomenon referred to as loss of plasticity. We identify a novel source of plasticity loss due to the growing anisotropy of weight matrices' singular values during training, and analyze this phenomenon both empirically and theoretically. To mitigate this issue, we introduce SingularClip, a procedure that periodically clips the singular values of all weight matrices. We show that SingularClip performs strongly against baselines across a range of tasks in both continual supervised learning and deep reinforcement learning.
core_methodology: Addresses neural network plasticity loss in nonstationary environments by controlling weight matrix singular value growth through periodic clipping (SingularClip). Methodology tested in both continual supervised learning and deep reinforcement learning settings.
data_sources: Experimental validation done on standard RL benchmarks and continual learning tasks (image classification, Atari games) rather than financial data, but method is data-agnostic.
alpha_potential: Could help maintain model performance when adapting to regime shifts in financial markets, especially for RL-based trading systems that suffer from concept drift. Theoretically applicable to momentum strategy decay in changing volatility regimes.
title_cn: SingularClip：防止频谱崩溃以保持持续学习和强化学习中的可塑性
summary_cn: 该论文提出SingularClip方法，通过周期性裁剪权重矩阵的奇异值来防止神经网络在非平稳任务中失去学习能力。对于量化交易中基于深度强化学习的策略在市场和波动机制转换时维持性能具有潜在应用价值。

title: Vector Symbolic Policy Gradient
summary: We answer this question with Vector-Symbolic Policy Gradient (VSPG), a discrete-action actor that represents each action by a unit-norm hypervector and scores it by similarity to the encoded state. Under the standard softmax policy-gradient surrogate, we prove that its update is exactly advantage-weighted hypervector bundling followed by normalization, and therefore supports standard advantage estimators. We further show that each trained action hypervector is a fixed-size compressed kernel memory, storing an advantage-weighted kernel expansion over visited states and transferring evidence according to the encoder-induced similarity. This provides a concrete mechanism that can support sample-efficient learning without increasing inference-time memory. Finally, for bipolar action memories, we prove that greedy action selection is stable under random bit flips, with failure probability decaying exponentially in the hypervector dimension. VSPG thus connects VSA action memories, log-linear policy gradients, and kernel policy search while providing a quantitative robustness guarantee.
core_methodology: Vector-Symbolic Policy Gradient (VSPG) uses hyperdimensional vector representations for actions and states, with policy updates performed via advantage-weighted hypervector bundling and normalization. It also leverages kernel memory for efficient learning.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify the data sources, but the methodology is general and could be applied to financial data such as price series or trading signals.
alpha_potential: The method's robustness to noise and its efficient learning mechanism could be leveraged for developing stable trading strategies, particularly in noisy or high-frequency trading environments.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Structure-Aware Numerical Reasoning in LLaMA 3.1 8B
summary: Recent work has shown that large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong numerical sequence modeling capabilities and show promise in time-series prediction. While LLMs display in-context learning capabilities, the mechanisms with which they accomplish time-series prediction remain unclear. Specifically, whether they truly understand the underlying structure, which at a minimum requires reasoning over first differences in the sequence of numbers. To study this, we investigate Llama 3.1-8B from a mechanistic interpretability point of view. Mechanistic interpretability is an emerging field concerned with the reverse engineering of the algorithms learned by neural networks such as LLMs. To assess Llamas' numerical sequence modeling capabilities and to facilitate our mechanistic interpretability analysis, we create a sequence modeling task that cannot be solved without picking up structural cues. Specifically, we sample n random numbers and repeat them with an offset. We find that Llama displays strong performance on our tasks suggesting that it can pick up on the underlying structure. To understand the mechanisms that allow it to do so, we perform probing experiments and activation patching based counterfactual analysis. Probing reveals that the model computes and stores first differences in its internal representations without explicit supervision, indicating that it tracks structural information about the sequence. Activation patching reveals that Llama retrieves the relevant first-difference with a mechanism similar to an induction circuit and subsequently adds it to the current value. Notably, our work represents one of the first studies to identify this form of concept induction in LLMs.
core_methodology: The paper employs mechanistic interpretability to understand how LLMs like LLaMA 3.1 8B model numerical sequences, specifically focusing on their ability to track first differences and structural cues in sequences. This involves probing experiments and activation patching to reverse-engineer the model's internal mechanisms.
data_sources: The study uses synthetic numerical sequences created by sampling random numbers and repeating them with an offset, designed to test structural understanding in sequence modeling.
alpha_potential: The findings suggest that LLMs can inherently model structural relationships in numerical sequences, which could be adapted for time-series prediction in financial markets, such as identifying patterns in price or volume data. However, the direct application to real-world trading requires further validation with market data.
title_cn: LLaMA 3.1 8B 对结构感知数值推理的机制可解释性研究
summary_cn: 本研究通过逆向工程分析LLaMA 3.1 8B在数值序列建模中的内部机制，发现其能够自动跟踪一阶差分和结构线索，这对金融时间序列预测（如价格或成交量模式识别）具有潜在应用价值，但需进一步的市场数据验证。

title: FinRCA-Bench: Benchmarking Evidence Retrieval and Reasoning for Financial AI Systems
summary: Large language models are increasingly used to support financial operations, but their apparent reasoning performance can depend on whether they receive the right evidence. In financial reconciliation, the evidence needed for diagnosis is distributed across invoices, purchase orders, approvals, allocations, payments, ledger entries, and bank activity, linked by transactional relationships rather than textual similarity. End-to-end accuracy can therefore conflate evidence access with reasoning quality. We introduce FinRCA-Bench, a deterministic synthetic benchmark of 2,250 accounts-payable-to-bank reconciliation cases spanning 14 operational tables, including 1,500 injected failures across 15 causal categories and 750 legitimate or hard-negative cases. Root-cause labels and record-level evidence contracts are hidden from the model, allowing retrieval to be evaluated independently of answer correctness. We compare Rules/SQL, classical machine learning, dense semantic retrieval, deterministic relational expansion, and Typed Provenance Graph Retrieval (TPGR), a typed traversal restricted to persisted transaction relationships. Rules/SQL reaches 84.97% held-out exact accuracy and classical ML reaches 95.44%. Holding the reasoning model, prompt, and generation settings fixed while changing only retrieval increases macro required-record recall from 0.83% to 77.70% and exact 16-class accuracy from 2.05% to 72.44%. Structural retrieval failures outnumber reasoning failures with sufficient retrieval by 95 to 15; 254 correct predictions occur despite incomplete retrieval, and strict returned-evidence contract accuracy is only 5.72%. On FinRCA-Bench, retrieval architecture strongly shapes observed AI-system performance, and a correct root-cause label is a weak proxy for an auditable diagnosis.
core_methodology: The paper introduces FinRCA-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating evidence retrieval and reasoning in financial AI systems, focusing on root cause analysis in financial reconciliation. It compares various methods including Rules/SQL, classical ML, dense semantic retrieval, deterministic relational expansion, and Typed Provenance Graph Retrieval (TPGR).
data_sources: Synthetic benchmark of 2,250 accounts-payable-to-bank reconciliation cases across 14 operational tables, including invoices, purchase orders, approvals, allocations, payments, ledger entries, and bank activity.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to improve the accuracy of root cause analysis in trading reconciliation processes, potentially reducing operational risks and improving efficiency in trading operations. However, the direct link to alpha generation in trading strategies is limited.
title_cn: FinRCA-Bench评估标准: 金融AI系统中证据检索与推理的基准测试
summary_cn: 该论文提出了FinRCA-Bench,一个用于评估金融AI系统中证据检索和推理能力的基准测试,重点关注财务对账中的根因分析。其方法可应用于提升交易对账准确性,降低操作风险,但对于直接的交易策略阿尔法生成关联性有限。

title: Multi-stage neural operator learning with application for convolutions
summary: Convolution integrals widely exist in applications, and to enable fast and accurate computations, this paper introduces two general multi-stage neural operator learning frameworks. The first, Deep Collocation Neural Operator (DCNO), is a supervised approach that iteratively refines the operator approximation by learning residuals from input-output data pairs. The second, Deep Galerkin Neural Operator (DGNO), is an unsupervised framework applicable when the target operator can be represented by a PDE, leveraging the weak form of the PDE residual for training. Both methods progressively construct basis operators through multiple training stages to enrich the approximation space, leading to significantly improved accuracy over standard one-shot operator learning. We provide theoretical analysis for their approximation capabilities and implement them for learning convolutions. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that both DCNO and DGNO achieve high accuracy, approaching machine precision under single float for convolution problems, and offer substantial efficiency gains for numerous queries or parametric variations compared to traditional solvers. We also extend these frameworks to handle multi-input operator learning scenarios involving variations in both the density and kernel of a convolution.
core_methodology: The paper introduces two multi-stage neural operator learning frameworks: Deep Collocation Neural Operator (DCNO) for supervised learning and Deep Galerkin Neural Operator (DGNO) for unsupervised learning. These methods iteratively refine operator approximations for convolution integrals, leveraging residuals from input-output data pairs or PDE representations.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on convolution integrals, which could be adapted for financial time series or signal processing applications.
alpha_potential: Potential applications include improving signal processing in high-frequency trading or enhancing convolution-based models for financial time series analysis. The high accuracy and efficiency gains could be leveraged for real-time trading systems.
title_cn: 多阶段神经算子学习及其在卷积中的应用
summary_cn: 该论文提出了两种多阶段神经算子学习框架（DCNO和DGNO），用于高效准确地近似卷积积分。这些方法通过迭代优化算子近似，可应用于金融时间序列的信号处理和高频交易策略，提升模型的实时性和准确性。

title: Converting Expert Deliberation into Financial Signals Through A Context-Aware NLP Pipeline
summary: We introduce the CDSP (context-conditional deliberation signal pipeline), converting an investment committee's meeting transcripts into structured predictive features. CDSP segments the meeting transcripts into topical chunks, assigns asset-class context labels using a large language model (LLM), maps financial keywords to a pre-determined taxonomy of labels, and constructs complementary features: sentiment polarity and mention frequency. This feature engineering framework is applied to a dataset spanning 48 monthly committee meetings to predict if global equities will perform better or worse than global bonds in the following month. In experiments with engineered features, raw transcript text, sentence embeddings, and combined representations, the prediction accuracy ranges from 62% to 73%, compared to always choosing stocks, which outperforms bonds 60.4% of the time. The best (73% accurate) model combines sentence embeddings with engineered CDSP features, achieving a 0.73 F1 score (although this is not statistically significant compared to always choosing stocks). Sentiment carries a stronger signal than mention frequency for several taxonomy categories. These findings suggest that experts' deliberations may contain forward-looking information that context-aware NLP can extract.
core_methodology: Context-aware NLP pipeline combining LLM-based context labeling, financial keyword mapping, sentiment analysis, and mention frequency to extract structured features from investment committee meeting transcripts.
data_sources: 48 monthly investment committee meeting transcripts (unstructured text data) for generating predictive signals about equity vs bond performance.
alpha_potential: Seeks to extract latent forward-looking information from expert deliberations by contextualizing unstructured text data - potentially capturing qualitative insights not reflected in market prices.
title_cn: 通过上下文感知的 NLP 处理流程将专家研讨内容转化为金融信号
summary_cn: 本研究开发了CDSP流程，通过大型语言模型对投资委员会会议记录进行上下文标注、金融关键词映射及情感分析，构建预测股市/债市表现的量化信号。在48个月度会议上测试显示73%预测准确率，表明专家讨论中可能含有未被定价的前瞻信息。

title: Grouping the Stochastic Machine: Precision, Not Capability, as the Frontier Metric for AI Systems
summary: Frontier language models are compared, marketed, and benchmarked on capability -- what their best or average output can achieve. I argue this measures the wrong axis. The models have saturated accuracy: their mean output lands on the target. What now separates one system from another in practice is precision: how tightly concentrated their outputs are around that target across repeated, identical requests. Borrowing the marksman's distinction, capability is where the average shot lands; reliability is the size of the group. I make three claims. First, precision, not capability, is the frontier differentiator between systems, and benchmark culture systematically fails to measure it, reporting central tendency rather than spread. Second, precision is measurable, cheaply and without circularity, by running a fixed suite of deterministically scored tasks many times at fixed temperature and computing the per-task consistency of outcomes -- no model-in-the-loop grader required. Third, the measurement is not merely descriptive but decision-guiding: it separates consistent failures (a tight group off-centre, correctable by the operating discipline of Paper 1 -- a sight adjustment) from scattered failures (a wide group, correctable only by changing the model or its sampling -- a rifle problem). I define a grouping metric, specify a harness, and show how tracking a human-AI pair's grouping over time yields the compounding signal that Paper 1's field study requires. A first real run, since replicated, illustrates both the method and its most important limit: one measured gap was closed completely by a single rule (0/5 -> 5/5), while a suite of tasks authored from the rules themselves found no value, because a frontier model already embodies explicit good practice -- establishing that a discipline's worth is found by measurement on real work, not constructed from its own rulebook.
core_methodology: The paper proposes evaluating AI systems based on precision (consistency of outputs around a target) rather than capability (average output quality). It introduces a metric for measuring precision and a method for tracking consistency over time.
data_sources: Not explicitly specified, but implied to be any dataset used for benchmarking AI models, potentially including financial datasets if applied to quantitative trading.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to improve the consistency of AI-driven trading signals, reducing variance in model outputs and potentially enhancing strategy reliability. However, the direct application to financial markets is not demonstrated.

title: L\'evy Attention: Single-Pass Predictive Uncertainty for Continuous-Time Attention
summary: Deep models for irregularly-sampled time series answer queries at arbitrary continuous timestamps, yet report nothing about how far each answer should be trusted. We show the attention layer itself can close that gap: with the right stochastic formulation, the pass that makes each prediction also reports, in closed form and at no extra cost, how far it should be trusted. We introduce L\'evy Attention, a cross-attention operator whose output is a stochastic integral against an inhomogeneous Poisson random measure: query-key compatibilities assemble an intensity over a continuous (time x channel) index space, the measure scatters atoms under it, and the output averages an interpolated value field at those atoms. In expectation it reduces to a mollified cosine-kernel attention, so it replaces a softmax layer and trains with exact gradients. What softmax discards, the Poisson construction preserves in closed form: the evidence $\Lambda_q$ (total compatibility mass) and the disagreement $\mathrm{tr}\,\Sigma_V(q)$ (value spread). An exact variance identity makes their combination $\hat\sigma(q)=\sqrt{\mathrm{tr}\,\Sigma_V(q)\,\varphi(\Lambda_q)}$ the root-mean-square deviation of the sampled operator, emitted by the deterministic pass with no trained head. Empirically, disagreement carries the signal, while the evidence factor swings from uninformative on dense data to strongly informative on sparse. On t-PatchGNN the operator swap costs at most 5.6% accuracy against a matched control and nothing on the sparsest dataset. The free disagreement signal improves on 20-pass MC dropout across matched five-seed suites, and $\hat\sigma$ scales a calibrated Gaussian whose zero-sample CRPS beats a fifty-draw sampler; a split-conformal wrapper reaches nominal coverage at every level, and one pass ranks 3,383 unseen patients by trust in 1.4 seconds.
core_methodology: Lévy Attention introduces a stochastic cross-attention operator that outputs predictive uncertainty estimates alongside predictions.
